card.title: FORGED IN FIRE
card.text: Give a unit a random combat keyword it doesn't have. Draw a card if it now has 2 or more.
card.flavorText: The Soviet Union’s Red Army emerged from the crucible of early WWII battles as a hardened and transformed force. In 1941, when Operation Barbarossa began, the Soviet military was poorly prepared for the scale and speed of the German invasion. Command structures were in disarray, equipment was insufficient or outdated, and morale plummeted as entire armies were encircled and destroyed. Yet by 1943, a different army stood on the Eastern Front. Harsh lessons learned from catastrophic defeats at Kiev, Vyazma, and Kharkov had forged new strategies, stronger leadership, and greater coordination between infantry, armor and artillery. Training improved rapidly. Factories relocated beyond the Urals churned out vast numbers of T-34 tanks, Il-2 aircraft, and Katyusha rocket launchers, overwhelming German forces with sheer volume. The pivotal battles of Stalingrad and Kursk were not only victories but demonstrations of a maturing military machine shaped by relentless struggle. Soviet soldiers, once hastily mobilized and under-equipped, became experienced and determined, capable of executing complex operations on a continental scale. The Red Army which drove into Berlin in 1945 was not the same force that had fled from Minsk in 1941. It had been forged in fire.
